description: Which order global setup runs in, and which project's config a shared hook gets (T9.15): Jest builds the list of hook paths from allTests, which is sorted by its sequencer across every project, not in the config's order. Three projects, listed a, b, c; c's test file is the largest, then b's, then a's, so with no history the sequenced list is c, b, a. Project c names b's hook files (the same absolute path), so that hook runs once, with the projectConfig of the first test that names it, which is c's; a's own hook runs after it; the root hook, which no project names, gets the first test's config, again c's. The teardowns run in the same order. Each hook appends a line to order.txt, which the black-box run captures. The projects come from --projects, because the recorder reserves the config key; they and the hooks are plain JavaScript, because a project's own config has no transformer for TypeScript.
